Remineralization is mineral restoration of the hydroxyapa-
tite in dental enamel. Casein phosphopeptide-amorphous 
calcium phosphate (CPP-ACP) is a substance that promotes 
remineralization of enamel surfaces (Cochrane et al, 2012). It is 
currently available as an ingredient trademarked as Recaldent 
(Cadbury Enterprises, Australia) in some brands of chewing 
gum (http://www.recaldent.com/c_faq.asp).
Factors Affecting Cariogenicity of Food
Cariogenicity also is influenced by the volume and quality of 
saliva; the sequence, consistency, and nutrient composition of 
the foods eaten; dental plaque buildup; and the genetic predis-
position of the host to decay.
Form and Consistency
The form and consistency of a food have a significant effect on 
its cariogenic potential and pH-reducing or buffering capacity. 
Food form determines the duration of exposure or retention 
time of a food in the mouth, which, in turn, affects how long 
the decrease in pH or the acid-producing activity will last.
